body: Confirmed, and deleting just the PNG and import from the zip causes the web editor to load successfully.

I can confirm on Edge browsers and I also explicitly set the png's `Detect 3D` option from `VRAM Compress` -> `Disabled` and the web editor still froze.

I also tested replacing the .PNG file with a .JPG and the JPG was loading VERY slowly, hanged at 40% after 5 minutes, and then the web editor completely froze after some time.

One last thing to note, I initially tried importing with the JPG version of the project directly after trying with the PNG project and it froze immediately. Only after clearing the Web Editor’s IndexedDB from the dev tools tab did I get some loading to happen with the JPG version.

So perhaps there's some issue with the IndexedDB as well. But overall, something wrong with the import pipeline. I'll look into how the Web Editor handles this and figure out recent changes that could be causing this and some possible fixes.
MRP with the JPG: [Test-JPG-Web-Import.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23483187/Test-JPG-Web-Import.zip)

From what I understand, web editor is single threaded and asset import thus will freeze trying to load the png. Also I noticed there's some recent changes that causes more IndexedDB syncs to occur even when project is already loaded, which can cause a deadlock situation when it's trying to sync but also trying to load assets like a png and jpg.

However, even if we enable multiple threads it may stop the freezing from happening but the png may still take forever to load on the separate thread.

This may be a root cause https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/98150 on disabling threading here but still trying to find anything else that could be regressing the png loading for web editor.

What's a situation where the Web editor is compiled with thread support but only has one thread?

It should definitely support multithreading and has done so in the past, so if it doesn't work in current versions this might be a regression. Indeed OP reports it as working in 4.4.1 and not in 4.5.1, so this should be bisected instead of disabling multithreading.

I can confirm the bug, 4.5.1.stable freezes and 4.4.1.stable works fine with the MRP in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112072#issuecomment-3517955821 (probably OP's too but I just picked one to test). I did a pre-bisect with intermediate builds of the web editor from https://editor.godotengine.org/releases/, it seems the regression was introduced between 4.5.dev4 and 4.5.dev5. Relevant changelog with a number of Web changes (including adding SIMD support): https://godotengine.github.io/godot-interactive-changelog/#4.5-dev5 But the regression may also be caused by changing the Emscripten version, which seems to have happened around that time: https://github.com/godotengine/build-containers/pull/151 We upgraded from Emscripten 3.1.64 to 4.0.10 around the time we built 4.5-dev5, though I'm not 100% sure of the exact date. The above PR was opened on May 15 so I must have started doing tests and possibly the dev5 build with it, but it was merged on June 12 (which would then be for beta1 on June 18). Proposed testing procedure: - Compile 4.5-dev5 (64b09905c) with Emscripten 4.0.10 and confirm whether the regression is reproducible. - Compile 4.5-dev5 with Emscripten 3.1.64 and see if that fixes the regression. - If yes, try to compile latest `master` with Emscripten 3.1.64 to see if that would also still fix the bug, and thus confirm that we need to look into Emscripten changes for the culprit. If Emscripten isn't the culprit, then: - Compiling 4.5-dev5 (64b09905c) with Emscripten 3.1.64 and 4.5-dev4 (209a446e3) to confirm my bisection, and bisect further to find the culprit commit in Godot. Assigning @adamscott as the Web maintainer, but anyone is welcome to do the steps above to pinpoint the regression further.

Thanks for being thorough @akien-mga my changes had basically made this part of the web editor synchronous which isn't a correct solution given @adamscott and others have done work to make this work with multiple threads.

Here were some findings I had originally that may be relevant.

a7d18f51a2 had introduced a line which may inadvertedly set Web version of Godot to only have 1 thread (which was causing issue in a busy wait loops during import and filesystem scanning), i went off the assumption this was being hit and causing issues downstream:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a7d18f51a2806734858f238a0d101b8f8ac1db1b/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_os.js#L353-L360

Busy wait during file system operations here, which may cause blocking the browser the event loop now that I think about it (i'm not too familliar with how multiple threads and the typical async setups that web apps expects interact):

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c742d107e29b2c858ef8930760479deb413c68bc/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp#L3326-L3338

I didn't realize there was infrastructure already in place to support multithreaded workflows in Web Editor (though, given some of the changes in a7d18f51a2 i should've suspected that)

I'll try your proposed testing procedure to see if the update in emscripten could be causing issue since that's deff a big change warranting scrutiny.

Might be worth testing a local revert of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/a7d18f51a2806734858f238a0d101b8f8ac1db1b to confirm whether that's the one introducing the regression in Godot (and thus the Emscripten version is not relevant to investigate).

The logic of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a7d18f51a2806734858f238a0d101b8f8ac1db1b/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_os.js#L353-L360 reads to me like it's testing whether threads are not enabled (`typeof PThread === 'undefined'`) to set it to 1, so in a case where threads are enabled and supported it shouldn't be 1. But maybe the logic doesn't work as expected?

Interesting but at 1777be4444 it looks like they were potentially trying to set num of threads directly in a js block in the `editor.html` file, which indicates the logic in l`ibrary_godot_os.js` may not be working as intended:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1777be44440057576741e1dce450cfdbe7ba38d9/misc/dist/html/editor.html#L677-L680

> Lines 353 to 360 in [a7d18f5](/godotengine/godot/commit/a7d18f51a2806734858f238a0d101b8f8ac1db1b)
>  godot_js_os_thread_pool_size_get: function () { 
>  	if (typeof PThread === 'undefined') { 
>  		// Threads aren't supported, so default to `1`. 
>  		return 1; 
>  	} 
>   
>  	return GodotConfig.godot_pool_size; 
>  }, 
> reads to me like it's testing whether threads are not enabled (`typeof PThread === 'undefined'`) to set it to 1, so in a case where threads are enabled and supported it shouldn't be 1. But maybe the logic doesn't work as expected?

So `PThread` is a Emscripten object that only exists when the project is compiled with threads enabled. It's just faster to check its existence directly instead of creating a C++ callback for JS that returns `true` if `THREADS_ENABLED` is defined.

> Interesting but at [1777be4](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/1777be44440057576741e1dce450cfdbe7ba38d9) it looks like they were potentially trying to set num of threads directly in a js block in the `editor.html` file, which indicates the logic in l`ibrary_godot_os.js` may not be working as intended:
> 
> [godot/misc/dist/html/editor.html](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1777be44440057576741e1dce450cfdbe7ba38d9/misc/dist/html/editor.html#L677-L680)
> 
> Lines 677 to 680 in [1777be4](/godotengine/godot/commit/1777be44440057576741e1dce450cfdbe7ba38d9)
>  const clamp = (value, min, max) => Math.min(Math.max(value, min), max); 
>  // We need at least 6 free threads from the pool to start the editor. 
>  // At least 4 more will be reserved for the godot thread pool (3 is the bare minimum with the multithreaded variant of the servers). 
>  const concurrency = clamp(navigator.hardwareConcurrency ?? 1, 12, 24);

This part of the code sets the capabilities of the browser for threads for the editor. I tested out the values of `concurrency` here and `godot_js_os_thread_pool_size_get()`. The former returns `16` and the latter returns `5`, so both work as intended.

Ok. So I can reproduce if I try to load the MRP [Project.with.PNG.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23156435/Project.with.PNG.zip), but I cannot reproduce if I create a new project with [the same PNG used in the project](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77fe3457-c84b-4d96-bf3a-1ab4cb96040c).

I was even able to load [Catburglar](https://bitbucket.org/JohnGabrielUK/catburglar/src) (a 450MiB project once zipped) without any hitch.

So I don't think it's Emscripten or thread related.

As discussed on chat, I can reproduce this even with Catburglar. But you need to make sure to upload a source project without having pre-imported all assets on PC (so without `.godot` folder). So the 27MiB source zip of Catburglar reproduces the issue, unlike the 450MiB pre-imported one.

> Compiling 4.5-dev5 ([64b0990](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/64b09905c7b2877f8aef99d8b63e73e5d31acfb9)) with Emscripten 3.1.64 and 4.5-dev4 ([209a446](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/209a446e3657e6fd736b9b7589b94cbdaad2d854)) to confirm my bisection, and bisect further to find the culprit commit in Godot.

So I've been trying this, and I managed to confirm that the regression is in Godot. I found that LTO (`production=yes`) is important to trigger the issue. I've been testing with **Emscripten 3.1.64** for all builds, to rule out an Emscripten regression.

- Compiling with `scons p=web target=editor use_closure_compiler=yes` (no LTO): Both 4.5-dev4 and 4.5-dev5 commits work fine to import Catburglar.
- Compiling with `scons p=web target=editor use_closure_compiler=yes production=yes` (LTO, same as official builds): 4.5-dev4 works, but 4.5-dev5 is broken.

I'm testing locally with the `serve.py` helper to deploy on localhost, and run on Firefox.

Deploying the official builds for 4.5-dev4 and 4.5-dev5 locally with `serve.py` also reproduces these results.

It took me several attempts to manage to reproduce the regression reliably though. I think it's important to `git clean` between builds as otherwise not everything might properly get regenerated.

So basically I'm doing:
```
git clean -fxd
git checkout 209a446e3657e6fd736b9b7589b94cbdaad2d854
scons p=web target=editor use_closure_compiler=yes production=yes
cp -r bin/.web_zip ../web_zip_4.5-dev4
git clean -fxd
git checkout 64b09905c7b2877f8aef99d8b63e73e5d31acfb9
scons p=web target=editor use_closure_compiler=yes production=yes
cp -r bin/.web_zip ../web_zip_4.5-dev5
```

Then serve the copied folders with `platform/web/serve.py`. To make sure results are reproducible, I close the browser between each attempt, and restarted the Python script. Otherwise if you run into a deadlock with an affected version, it may invalidate doing another test in the same browser process as it's in a broken state.

---

Note: I first tried using latest Emscripten 4.0.22, but it fails compiling 4.5-dev5 with some LLVM internal compiler error. 4.5-dev4 compiles ok. That might also be a hint that we changed something in 4.5-dev5 that doesn't play nice with Emscripten. This should be investigated separately, especially after checking whether the issue is reproducible on `master`. It may be a regression in cutting edge Emscripten that should be reported upstream.
@akien-mga (about your note and just as a note also) I had the same error with 4.0.22, but 4.0.21 builds fine.

Note for testing: Another thing which impacts reproducibility is the browser cache. I just did a whole bisect with clean builds but reusing `bin/.web_zip` to deploy, and ended up with 100% good commits... until I tried on another browser to realize it's a caching issue.

I stop looking into it for now, but I strongly suspect #104458 is what causes the regression, and LTO might be messing up e.g. the visibilty of `PThread` from JS.

So now that I figured out the cache issue for testing, it's a bit easier to reproduce. To make sure my tests are consistent, I copy and rename `bin/.web_zip` after each build to have a unique path for each build I'm testing, and deploy them with `serve.py`.

Given the above hunch, I checked directly that 2df41d8144685f0c951476a85d48479fa91eb558 (merge commit of #104458) reproduces the issue, while its parent commit eb72ce2db4b67acbc77548e5a5a7f61af657660b doesn't.

I could also reproduce the issue with 2df41d8144685f0c951476a85d48479fa91eb558 compiled without LTO (`production=no`), so this isn't a LTO problem as I suspected earlier. This makes testing easier as linking time with LTO is super long.

CC @marcosc90

Some data points from my system (Firefox on Fedora 43, 16 cpu procs, Emscripten 4.0.23):
- `OS::get_singleton()->get_processor_count()` returns `2`
- `OS::get_singleton()->get_default_thread_pool_size()` returns `5`

When no thread count is specified, WorkerThreadPool uses `OS::get_singleton()->get_default_thread_pool_size()` i.e. 5 in my case. Before #104458, this function was hardcoded to `1` on Web, and so this change seems to break things for the Web editor.

So in the end the regression is that #104458 enabled multi-threaded import on the web editor, which was disabled previously due to the default WTP thread pool size.

So #114410 wasn't a bad solution in the end, I think re-disabling this for the Web editor makes sense, at least as a stopgap measure until we can figure out how to make multi-threaded import work on web.

There might be other uses of WTP that are now breaking after #104458, so we should keep an eye out for that.

Yeah my PR, though a temp solution, does allow Web editor to be aligned with the rest of Godot version-wise until a proper fix is tested and release.

I believe the busy-wait loop I mentioned may be *part* of the issue. web/JS typically expects asynchronous execution or at least multithreaded workloads to be done on worker threads instead of the main thread which can prevent browser event loop from processing UI, input, and async completion callbacks.

While working on my PR, the filesystem operations were the only things blocking the editor that I can identity so the above, if my suspicions are correct, may also fix the issue.
